_comment: What the agent and the server must agree on. They are separate Go modules,
so neither can import the other's constants and nothing but this file ties
them together. Both test suites read it: apps/agent/internal/client and
apps/server/internal/api each assert their own side matches.
Adding a value here is not enough. The agent test fails if it can emit a
value this file omits, and the server test fails if it rejects one this
file lists, so a change has to land on all three or the build breaks.
_terminalMessageTypesComment: Every message type that crosses the terminal WebSocket. The server sends
open/input/keys/reply/resize/close to the agent and the agent sends
output/exit/error back; status and error also go to the browser. 'keys'
carries raw keystrokes; nothing screens them on the way, because the
server reads the shell's echo and applies the deny policy when a Return
arrives. 'reply' carries the console emulator's answer to a terminal
_logCaptureComment: What a read may ask a node for. 'host' and 'container' exist because
on a working host the journal is almost entirely one application's
output, so reading everything answers with that and buries the host.
Container output carries no syslog facility, so naming every facility
selects the host alone; conmon is the monitor all container output
passes through, so it selects the other half. logCapturePriorities is
the severity band, which only a read can select on: the live view
carries named senders rather than a severity range.
_logStreamComment: The live view is an allowlist of senders, not a severity floor. Severity is
chosen by whoever wrote the program and they are careless in both
directions: measured over a day, every sudo session and account change was
logged at info, 50 of 61 kernel lines sat below warning including a process
crash, and a container's startup banner reached the journal as an error
because the runtime maps stderr to err whatever the text says. Naming the
senders says what is meant; everything else waits on the node for a read.
_guestMetricAttributesComment: The attribute names a guest's absolute figures are stored under, written by
the container and VM metric paths and read by the console. They are listed
here because the two paths disagreed: the container path wrote usage under
memoryBytes while the VM path wrote the allowance there, and the console --
reading both the VM's way -- showed a container as '0 B / 8.2 MB'.
memoryUsedBytes is what is in use; memoryBytes is what that is a share of.
